title: It began with a game
back: In 1654 Pascal and Fermat wrote to each other about a gambler's puzzle. Their letters are usually counted as the start of probability.

title: Probability of an event
back: The outcomes must be equally likely. The answer is always between 0 and 1.

title: Not E
back: Use it for 'not', and for 'at least one' = 1 − P(none).

title: The two ends of the scale
back: Getting 8 on a die: 0. Getting a number less than 7: 1.

title: Two dice: 36 outcomes
back: Sum 7 is the most likely (6 ways). (2, 6) and (6, 2) are different outcomes.

title: The pack of 52 cards
back: 4 suits of 13; 26 red, 26 black; 12 face cards (J, Q, K); 4 aces.

title: Coins
back: Three coins: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH, HTT, THT, TTH, TTT.

title: At least one
back: Count the single case 'none' and subtract.

title: Cards or balls removed
back: The total changes: write the new total first.

title: Ways to get each sum
back: Sums 2 and 12 have 1 way each; the count rises to 6 ways for 7, then falls.
